assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correcting spherical aberration turned the transmission electron microscope from a diffraction-limited instrument into one that resolves atoms routinely, including light atoms, interfaces and defects. It is a clear invention with a concrete before and after, and its impact on materials physics, chemistry and nanoscience is broad and lasting. As a microscopist I judge it from daily practice, which is a strength but also a risk of bias toward my own field.
assessment.attribution: The decisive steps are the Rose hexapole and corrector design, the Haider-Urban-Rose implementation of the first working TEM corrector, and Urban's group demonstration of sub-angstrom imaging of materials. The three credited names map well onto theory, engineering and application. I would check whether the Krivanek-led STEM corrector, which is not among the credited names, makes the TEM-only framing too narrow.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of independent confirmation; commercial instruments worldwide rely on it. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Parallel STEM corrector work by other groups is not credited in this entry and could complicate the allocation.
Possible perceived closeness to my own research field; I rely on recollection of the history rather than independently verified facts.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened an entirely new platform (moire materials) for strongly correlated physics. It combines a clean theoretical idea with a striking experiment and has generated a very large field.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald supplied the continuum-model prediction; Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators supplied the decisive experiments. A prediction plus experiment pairing fits the prize format, though the first author of the 2018 experiments (Cao) and other contributors are not eligible under the three-person limit and not in the credited set.
assessment.maturity: Strongly replicated across many groups and materials in under a decade; the interpretation of the superconducting mechanism remains unsettled, although the existence of flat-band correlated phases is solid.
uncertainties: Origin of superconductivity is still debated.
Sample inhomogeneity (twist-angle disorder) complicates quantitative comparisons.
Earlier theoretical flat-band work by others may bear on priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Metal-halide perovskites went from a curiosity to a photovoltaic and optoelectronic material with efficiencies rivaling silicon in about a decade, and revealed unusual defect tolerance and carrier physics. Impact on energy materials is large, though the discovery is partly materials engineering and the physics part is still being clarified.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka's dye-sensitized perovskite cell, Park's solid-state cell and Snaith's thin-film and meso-superstructured work are the usual landmark steps. Credit is plausible for three but contested at the margins (Kojima, Segawa, Gratzel and others appear in the history).
assessment.maturity: Rapid replication and enormous activity; long-term stability and lead toxicity are unresolved, and the Nobel-level discovery might be judged as insufficiently settled for a physics prize.
uncertainties: Operational stability and commercialization are unresolved.
The credit boundary with the Kojima and Gratzel contributions is unclear.
Physics versus chemistry framing for this committee.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Predicting the quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators and then observing it in HgTe established topological band theory as a central organizing concept in condensed matter. It is original, conceptually clear and has had a very large impact on materials and device thinking.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction and introduced the Z2 invariant; Molenkamp's group delivered the experimental realization (with Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang's HgTe proposal and Konig et al.). The three-person configuration is reasonable, although Bernevig, Zhang and others have strong claims, so allocation is delicate.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with multiple independent confirmations and a broad materials family; the 2016 prize recognized earlier topological phase theory, which may reduce the novelty weight of this follow-up.
uncertainties: Competing credit claims (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu, Moore, Balents, Roy, Qi-Kun Xue) cannot be fully accommodated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller's proposals for trapped-ion quantum computing and for quantum simulation in optical lattices defined much of experimental quantum information and many-body quantum simulation. Their ideas were tested directly by experiments that now underpin the field.
assessment.attribution: The two-person pairing is natural and well recognized, as the theoretical origin of the ion-trap gate and of lattice simulators. Experimental implementers (Blatt, Wineland, Bloch and others) are outside this entry; the prior 2012 prize to Wineland partly overlaps in subject matter.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by multiple experimental platforms over 25 years. Timing is fine, but the topic is adjacent to earlier prizes.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize and the 2022 quantum-information prize.
Prize-worthiness as pure theory depends on how directly experiments are attributed to the proposals.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of iron-pnictide superconductivity in 2008 opened a second high-temperature superconductor family, with critical temperatures above 50 K and a rich interplay of magnetism and superconductivity. As a materials physicist I regard this as a clear, impactful discovery, though practical consequences are limited.
assessment.attribution: Hosono's group made the discovery (LaFeAsO with fluorine doping) and so the attribution is clear for a single laureate, although the quick follow-up by Chinese groups raised Tc substantially and could prompt arguments for broader credit.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced rapidly and extensively; the pairing mechanism is still debated and applications remain limited. Timing is acceptable but not pressing.
uncertainties: Follow-up work from other groups (for example Ren, Chen and colleagues) could affect fairness of a single-laureate award.
The credited names list only one person.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* are direct visual evidence of black holes, a landmark in both instrumentation (VLBI at 1.3 mm) and astrophysics. Importance and public impact are high, although the discovery is an observation and interpretation of a predicted object rather than a surprise.
assessment.attribution: The collaboration has hundreds of members; Falcke proposed the shadow concept, Doeleman led the array development and the collaboration, and Zensus was a leading figure in VLBI. Fair attribution within a very large team is difficult, and the three-person rule makes any selection contestable.
assessment.maturity: Strong for M87* and Sgr A* with consistent results, although polarization and dynamics studies are still evolving and the interpretation depends on modelling.
uncertainties: Large-collaboration credit is hard to reduce to three people.
Image reconstruction and interpretation depend on modelling assumptions I cannot independently verify.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical readout and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond created a room-temperature solid-state qubit and a broad family of quantum sensors, with applications from nanoscale magnetometry to biology. From my materials perspective the defect physics and the imaging of single defects are especially compelling.
assessment.attribution: Jelezko and Wrachtrup did the early single-NV optical detection and coherent control; Lukin's group contributed to coherent control and quantum sensing proposals and experiments. Other leaders (Awschalom, Hanson, Jelezko-Wrachtrup, Walsworth, Budker and others) have significant claims, and the exact credit is delicate. Note that Lukin also appears in several other candidates.
assessment.maturity: Replicated widely and still maturing as sensing technology advances; fundamental discovery is mature, whereas applications are still developing.
uncertainties: Competing credit claims from Awschalom, Hanson and others for spin control and quantum networks.
Whether sensing or qubit control is the prize-worthy core is unclear.
